title: Is it a bird…?
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars swirl in long trails around the sky's south pole above ESO's La Silla Observatory. The picture combines a long series of separate images, so Earth's rotation shows up as the stars' circling paths.

The MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope's silver dome stands in the foreground. Behind it are the ESO 1-metre Schmidt telescope in its white dome and the boxy New Technology Telescope building, and at the back the ESO 3.6-metre telescope's double domes sit beside a smaller neighbour, the now-retired Coudé Auxiliary Telescope.

Three horizontal streaks cross the sky from left to right. They do not turn with the stars, which shows they are much closer to home. They are aeroplanes. The observatory sits close to a fairly busy flight path, and these trails come from aircraft flying from Calama to Santiago.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape made by combining many exposures at La Silla, which turns stars into trails. No other camera settings are published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points, but combining many exposures records their slow circling as long trails.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO Photo Ambassador Alexandre Santerne took the photograph. When he is not photographing observatories, he travels the world, Chile included, for his research on planets orbiting other stars. Stars appear to circle the sky's poles because Earth spins on its axis.
alt: Long star trails curving around the sky's south pole above several telescope domes and buildings, with three straight horizontal streaks from aircraft crossing the sky.
